record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical two-dimensional conformal field theory
record.original_question: Can one study the moduli space of two-dimensional conformal field theories by defining topological and geometric structures on it, and prove that rational conformal field theories are isolated points in this moduli space?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Study the moduli space of conformal field theories. Give topological and geometric structures on the moduli space. Prove that rational conformal field theories are isolated points in the moduli space.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ denote the moduli space of two-dimensional conformal field theories (CFTs), where each point represents an equivalence class of unitary 2D CFTs (parametrized, for instance, by the central charge together with the data of the chiral algebra, the spectrum of primary fields, conformal weights, and operator product expansion coefficients, modulo isomorphism). A CFT is called rational if its chiral algebra has only finitely many inequivalent irreducible representations and its partition function decomposes as a finite sum of holomorphic times anti-holomorphic characters.

(a) Equip $\mathcal{M}$ with natural topological and geometric structures (for example, a topology induced by deformation theory of CFTs via exactly marginal operators, and a Riemannian or Kähler structure given by the Zamolodchikov metric on the space of marginal deformations).

(b) Prove or disprove: with respect to such structures, every rational conformal field theory is an isolated point of $\mathcal{M}$, i.e., there exists a neighborhood of any rational CFT in $\mathcal{M}$ containing no other rational CFT.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of defining topological/geometric structures on the moduli space of 2D CFTs and proving that rational CFTs form isolated (or at least non-dense) points remains an active research topic. Recent work (Benjamin–Keller–Ooguri–Zadeh, 2020/2021) investigates the distribution of rational points in CFT moduli spaces and conjectures that rational CFTs are generally not dense (possibly finite for Calabi–Yau n-folds with n > 2), but a general proof that every rational CFT is isolated has not been established. The problem appears open in general.

status_evidence.title: On Rational Points in CFT Moduli Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: We investigate the distribution of points in moduli spaces of 2d CFTs that correspond to theories with enhanced chiral algebras, in particular rational CFTs.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies the distribution of rational CFTs in moduli space, indicating the problem is still active and conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Rational Conformal Field Theories and Complex Multiplication
status_evidence.snippet: Studies special arithmetic structure of rational points in CFT moduli spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization of rational CFTs as isolated arithmetic points is partially explored but not proven in general.
